title: WeaveSignal
author: The WeaveSignal contributors
tagline: An internet radio and video studio: a live room with callers, the desk, playout, streams and chat

LISTENERS_DOMAIN.title: Listener stream
LISTENERS_DOMAIN.description: The listener stream (Ogg Opus), served by icecast.server behind this domain. It is not listed in any directory.

ROOM_DOMAIN.title: Live room signalling
ROOM_DOMAIN.description: LiveKit's signalling for presenters, guests and callers (WebSocket). Room access needs a short-lived token from the station.

PUBLIC_DOMAIN.title: Public pages
PUBLIC_DOMAIN.description: The station's public pages, outside Cloudron's login: the player with call-in and the live chat, invited guests' join page, the echo test, podcast feeds, show cards and episode files. The app's own domain stays for the studio.

LIVEKIT_MEDIA_PORT.title: Live room media (UDP)
LIVEKIT_MEDIA_PORT.description: LiveKit's one WebRTC media port (ADR-0023). Default 7882; a port in 52000-60000 or 443/udp are alternatives, and any free UDP port may be used. Avoid 50000-51000, Cloudron's own TURN relay range.

TURN_UDP_PORT.title: TURN over UDP
TURN_UDP_PORT.description: LiveKit's built-in TURN over UDP. Off by default: guests who cannot use the media port use TURN over TLS. Cloudron's own TURN holds 3478, so 3479 or 13478; any free UDP port may be used.

SOURCE_SRT_PORT.title: Hosts' own studios: SRT
SOURCE_SRT_PORT.description: SRT from a host's own software (OBS, vMix, ffmpeg) with a show key: the key id is the stream ID and its secret the passphrase (ADR-0280). Off by default; the ingest listens only while a show key exists. Default 9710; 19710 or 29710 are alternatives, and any free UDP port may be used.

SOURCE_WHIP_PORT.title: Hosts' own studios: WHIP
SOURCE_WHIP_PORT.description: WHIP's sound from a host's OBS (30 and later) with a show key: the offer goes to https://<public domain>/whip/<key id> with the key's secret as the Bearer Token, and the sound to this port (ICE-lite, no STUN or TURN). Needs the public domain. Off by default; the ingest listens only while a show key exists. Default 9712; 19712 or 29712 are alternatives, and any free UDP port may be used.

TURN_TLS_PORT.title: TURN over TLS
TURN_TLS_PORT.description: LiveKit's built-in TURN over TLS, for guests on networks that block UDP and for GrapheneOS's browser (ADR-0059). On Cloudron the default is 15349, because Cloudron's own TURN holds 5349 (ADR-0106); any free TCP port may be used.

LIVEKIT_TCP_PORT.title: Live room media over TCP
LIVEKIT_TCP_PORT.description: LiveKit's ICE over TCP, a fallback when UDP is blocked. Off by default: TURN over TLS covers the same guests. Default 7881; any free TCP port may be used.

SOURCE_ICECAST_PORT.title: Hosts' own studios: Icecast
SOURCE_ICECAST_PORT.description: Icecast sources from a host's own software (BUTT, Mixxx, RadioDJ) with a show key (ADR-0280). Off by default; the ingest listens only while a show key exists. Default 8005; 18005 or 28005 are alternatives, and any free TCP port may be used.

set-up-the-station.message: Set the station up. Open the app's own address with `/setup/` on the end and sign in with `CONTROL_ADMIN_TOKEN` from `/app/data/secrets.env` (open it with the File Manager). Give the station its name, a takedown contact (call-in stays closed until you do), its jurisdiction and its look.

make-yourself-an-admin.message: Make yourself an admin. In the studio app choose **Use the station key instead**, add yourself under **Settings > Staff**, then sign in as yourself. Give each member of staff an account of their own there.

choose-who-hears-the-stream.message: Choose who may hear the stream. It is unlisted but open to anyone with its address. To ask for a password, set `LISTENERS_AUTH=on` in `/app/data/weavesignal.env` and restart the app; it then asks for the user `listener` and `LISTENERS_PASSWORD` from `secrets.env`. The player page cannot play a stream that has a password.

open-the-ports.message: Open the public ports in the server's firewall and in any cloud firewall: the live room's media port (UDP), TURN over TLS, and any optional port you turned on.

hosts-own-studios.message: Only if hosts will send their shows from their own software: the two ports for it, Icecast (TCP) and SRT (UDP), are off until you turn them on in the app's **Location** settings. Open them in the firewall too. The station listens on them only once a show has a key.
